content.summary: A book from AKU faculty will narrate how surgical specialities evolved in Pakistan.

content.text: The story of how surgical specialities evolved in Pakistan is full of curious details and little-known facts, narrated in a book to be launched by faculty from the Aga Khan University. The upcoming publication was announced at the inaugural session of the 7th

'Evolution of Surgical Specialities in Pakistan: Chronicles from the Theatres and Beyond' is meant to be an invaluable resource for all surgeons and medical history buffs and a must-have for those related to healthcare in Pakistan. The editors include Drs Shahzad Shamim, Muhammad Rizwan Khan, Safdar Ali Shaikh and Syed Ather Enam.
The theme of this year's surgical conference focuses on improving surgical research in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

"Research in surgery has enabled surgeons to enhance the quality of healthcare and improve patient outcomes," said Dr Shahzad Shamim, chair of the organising committee. "We are also exploring what tools and methodologies are needed to improve surgical education and research, considering the availability of expertise, resources and technology in LMICs like Pakistan."

While the College of Physicians and Surgeons, Pakistan is the main certifying institution for surgeons, the public and private teaching hospitals bear the burden of responsibility for surgical education and training. But the capacity of the healthcare system in the country has not expanded at the pace of surgical care needs, and the COVID-19 pandemic has widened the gap further with financial implications on healthcare system, education and research.
"Additionally, the effects of new COVID variants like Omicron on healthcare facilities and workers are causing delays even in scheduled surgeries," said Dr Shamim.

The conference will explore how to deal with new challenges while keeping an eye on existing issues, addressing the shortage of trained surgical specialists, unequal distribution of trained surgeons in urban and rural areas and absence of a centralised, well-structured training body.
As a start, the Journal of the Pakistan Medical Association has collaborated with the organisers and published a special supplement on the conference with 26 papers on surgical research.

The three-day conference will feature more than 100 experts from around the world and several sessions, including keynote addresses by well-known surgical humanities author Henry Marsh, Executive Director of American College of Surgeons David B. Hoyt, and a dialogue with musician and the UN Goodwill Ambassador for HIV/AIDS Salman Ahmad.
AKU President Sulaiman Shahabuddin, Medical College Dean Adil Haider and Department of Surgery Chair Syed Ather Enam addressed the inaugural session.
